question.worked_solution:
Recall that a linear congruence $ax≡b\,(\text{mod}\,n)$ has a unique solution modulo $n$ if and only if $\text{gcd}(a,n)=1.$

In the given congruence, we have $a=40$ and $n=333$, where

$$
\text{gcd}(a,n)=\text{gcd}(40,333)=1.
$$

So, our congruence does indeed have a unique solution.

To find the solution, we need to multiply both sides of the equation by the multiplicative inverse of $40\,(\text{mod}\,333).$ To find the inverse of $40\,(\text{mod}\,333)$, use the extended Euclidean algorithm.

First, we apply the forward reduction:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}333 & = & 40\cdot 8 & + & 13 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  \\ 40 & = & 13\cdot 3 & + & 1\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Solving for the rightmost terms in the equations above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}13 & =333-40\cdot 8 \\ 1 & =40-13\cdot 3\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we back-substitute:

$$
\begin{aligned}1 & =40-13\cdot 3 \\  & =40-(333-40\cdot 8)\cdot 3 \\  & =40\cdot 25+333\cdot (-3)\end{aligned}
$$

We can write this result in modulo $333,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}40\cdot 25+333\cdot (-3) & ≡1 &  & (\text{mod}\,333) \\ 40\cdot 25 & ≡1 &  & (\text{mod}\,333)\end{aligned}
$$

So, $40\cdot 25≡1\,(\text{mod}\,333),$ which means that $25$ is the multiplicative inverse of $40$ (modulo $333$).

Now, multiplying both sides of our original congruence by $25,$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}40x & ≡7 &  & (\text{mod}\,333) \\ 25\cdot 40x & ≡25\cdot 7 &  & (\text{mod}\,333) \\ (25\cdot 40)x & ≡175 &  & (\text{mod}\,333) \\ 1\cdot x & ≡175 &  & (\text{mod}\,333) \\ x & ≡175 &  & (\text{mod}\,333)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x≡175\,(\text{mod}\,333).$
